facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He feels like he is running on fumes.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work involves long hours
facts.content: Daniel works as a project manager at a logistics company. He is thinking about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night. Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours.

facts.heading: Wakes up at 3 AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Headaches upon waking
facts.content: Daniel's head hurts when he wakes up at 3 AM.
facts.evidence: My head just hurts.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's symptoms
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, he's slower, he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Father is the strong one
facts.content: Daniel's father is always being the strong one.
facts.evidence: he's always being the strong one.

facts.heading: Drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's sister Hannah lives in Toronto. She calls their father every Sunday.
facts.evidence: My angry sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls of me. She calls him every Sunday.

facts.heading: Guilt about caregiving
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty about his role in caring for his father. He feels selfish to be tired when he is ill.
facts.evidence: He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Avoids sharing feelings
facts.content: Daniel does not say anything to anyone about his feelings. He does not say anything to Hannah either.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone. Not to Hanach either?

facts.heading: Does not disclose feelings
facts.content: Daniel tells Hannah he is fine when she asks how he is.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.heading: Desires to communicate truth
facts.content: Daniel wants to tell Hannah that he is not fine. He wants to tell her that some days he sits in a car park at a hospital for 10 minutes before.
facts.evidence: That I'm not fine. That some days I sit in a car park at a hospital for 10 minutes before

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests which were all normal. The GP said it is stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: GP advised no talk therapy
facts.content: The GP said Daniel had no time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: she said I hadn't got the time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked time
facts.content: A girlfriend named Claire booked time with Daniel. Claire said she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: A girlfriend booked her, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is very patient and makes Daniel tea. She does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire worries too
facts.content: Daniel can see that Claire is worrying about herself too.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's worrying about her too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped weekend plans
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel if he wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause stress
facts.content: The emails are a reason Daniel cannot say yes to plans. Daniel will have to respond to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a price. He cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Ran before October
facts.content: Daniel ran three years every Saturday morning for six years. He stopped about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I ran. I'm going to be three years every Saturday morning. I've done it for six years. And now? I stopped about two months ago.

facts.heading: Legs feel like lead
facts.content: Daniel's legs feel like lead after stopping running. He has not gone back.
facts.evidence: My legs feel like lead. And I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He cannot picture the time that would come from getting it back.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me. What would it mean to get some of that back? A lot, probably. Just can't picture the time that would come from.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast. Daniel answers them every time.
facts.evidence: Peterson. He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast. What do you do when one arrives? I answer it. Every time.

facts.heading: Fear of not answering
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that his boss will think he is not committed if he does not answer.
facts.evidence: Dan, he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: There is a restructuring this spring, and Daniel is afraid they will let him go. He is afraid his boss will think he would be relieved.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go. And if they did? I don't know. He'd think part of me would be relieved.

facts.heading: Fear of mortgage impact
facts.content: Daniel feels horrible about being relieved because he has a mortgage. He acknowledges both things can be true.
facts.evidence: And I'd feel horrible about being relieved. I have a mortgage. Both things can be true.

facts.heading: Moves apart from tiredness
facts.content: Daniel moves apart from tiredness and feels flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Slept in toilets
facts.content: Daniel slept at a colleague last week or nothing and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during sleep
facts.content: When Daniel slept, his heart was going and his hands were shaking.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Experienced heart attack
facts.content: Daniel experienced a heart attack that passed. He has experienced this a couple of times before.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed. Has it happened before? A couple of times.

facts.heading: Heart attack location
facts.content: Daniel experienced the heart attack on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing self
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing it or going to end up coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.

facts.heading: Wine consumption amount
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Effectiveness of wine
facts.content: The wine works for about an hour. Daniel feels it is not helping.
facts.evidence: It works for an hour. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Carrying burdens
facts.content: Daniel feels like he is listing everything wrong with him. He thinks he is carrying a great deal on his own.
facts.evidence: It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me. I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time.

facts.heading: Desire for sleep
facts.content: Daniel thinks that if he could sleep, he could probably cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything when working at the mines.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything. Not once.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks he would be seen as weak for being there. He wants to tell his grandfather he is not weak but tired.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here. That I'm not weak. Just very tired.

facts.heading: Willingness to try small steps
facts.content: Daniel was asked if he would be willing to try something small. He agreed.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small? Yeah, half past nine perhaps.

facts.heading: Proposed small action
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try switching off his phone for 20 minutes at half past nine.
facts.evidence: I could make it a dangles glare. The end of sofa.

facts.heading: Current feeling state
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.

facts.heading: Acknowledged difficulty speaking
facts.content: Daniel found it difficult to speak loudly.
facts.evidence: Very normal. It takes energy to say it loud loud.

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again next week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week?
